target.title: refactor(whatsapp): reuse SDK agent-tool utilities
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The WhatsApp call tool duplicated the SDK's JSON tool-result construction and manually managed the temporary directory, WAV write, and cleanup lifecycle for synthesized call audio.

## Why This Change Was Made

The call tool now imports `jsonResult` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results` and removes its local duplicate. It also uses `withTempWorkspace` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/temp-path`, writes `message.wav` through `workspace.write`, and executes MeowCaller within the workspace callback so the directory is cleaned up on success, command failure, timeout, cancellation, or another thrown error.

The validated TTS sample rate is carried into a local constant before entering the async workspace callback. Command arguments, timeout calculation, cancellation handling, per-account concurrency, result payloads, and MeowCaller error handling remain unchanged.

The focused call-tool test now verifies that the workspace directory uses mode `0700` and the synthesized WAV uses mode `0600` on platforms that enforce POSIX permissions. Existing assertions continue to verify the exact MeowCaller argument list and cleanup after successful and failed calls.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The WhatsApp call implementation now relies on the shared SDK utilities for tool results and private temporary-file lifecycle management.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/agent-tools-call.test.ts` — 11 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm lint:extensions` — passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Structured Codex autoreview — clean, no actionable findings
